input.candidate_name: coverage-preserving exploration reserve against theory-conditioned sampling lock-in

primary_sources.title: Against theory-motivated experimentation: Can random experimental choice lead to better theories?
observed: The study is a multi-agent computational model of active experimentation, theory construction and social learning over mixture-of-multivariate-Gaussian ground truths. Experiment 1 analyzed 9,060 completed simulations across varied contexts.
Actual performance is evaluated on 10,000 representative samples from the original ground-truth distribution rather than only on the agents' adaptively collected observations.

Relative to random, Appendix Table A1 actual-error coefficients are +582.24 disagreement+falsification, +720.45 disagreement+confirmation, +666.92 disagreement, +656.62 falsification, +1228.46 confirmation and +262.37 novelty; all are reported p<.001 for that linear-model coefficient table.
The paper reports random as best or tied for best actual ground-truth reconstruction at 50, 100, 150, 200, 250 and 300 collected observations and across the varied model contexts it tested.

Crucial treatment detail: every strategy except the pure-random baseline begins with 10 fully random observations and thereafter uses a constant 10% random exploration rate. Therefore the negative result is not a comparison of pure theory-conditioned sampling against a theory-conditioned policy with no exploration reserve; the tested nonrandom policies already contain a small fixed random reserve.

Theory-guided choice controls only the conditioning dimension/value for the next observation; the remaining dimensions are sampled from the ground-truth distribution conditional on that chosen value. The treatment is therefore narrower than arbitrary whole-experiment generation by an autonomous scientist.

The paper explicitly limits transport to other domains: its ground truths are high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures, measurement noise is absent, and sparse/low-dimensional/discrete causal structures may not retain the same advantage for random exploration.

primary_sources.title: Characterizing the robustness of Bayesian adaptive experimental designs to active learning bias
primary_sources.observed: Bayesian adaptive design can suffer active-learning bias under model misspecification; worse misspecification increases bias in the analyzed linear setting and the qualitative pattern is demonstrated in a simulated nonlinear preference-learning setting. It does not identify an exploration-reserve fraction for the 2026 scientist-agent candidate.

material_findings.claim: Theory-conditioned experiment choice can create an illusion of success by sampling less representative regions while performing worse on representative ground-truth evaluation.
material_findings.scope: The perceived-versus-actual reversal, coefficient signs and representative-ground-truth evaluation are directly supported by the primary article within its Gaussian-mixture simulation family. This is not a laboratory or LLM-scientist intervention.

material_findings.claim: The paper motivates adding a nonzero random or coverage-preserving exploration reserve to an otherwise theory-targeted scientist.
material_findings.scope: The tested nonrandom strategies already use 10 random burn-in observations plus a constant 10% random exploration rate and still underperform the pure-random baseline on actual performance. The paper therefore shows that this particular small fixed reserve is insufficient in its regimes; it does not establish that merely adding a reserve fixes lock-in, nor identify a sufficient reserve size or adaptive arbitration rule.

material_findings.claim: Candidate promotion should be judged on representative or held-out coverage rather than only the adaptively collected sample.
material_findings.scope: The paper evaluates actual performance using 10,000 representative samples from a known ground-truth distribution. That supports separating acquisition data from representative adjudication. It is not a finite reusable-holdout protocol and does not establish adaptive-reuse-safe holdout governance.

material_findings.claim: Random experimentation universally dominates targeted experimentation.
material_findings.scope: The authors explicitly decline a universal recommendation and flag sparse/low-dimensional/discrete causal structures, measurement noise and practical cost/domain constraints as outside or potentially different regimes.

downstream_implication: Keep candidate_068 as negative evidence against allocating the entire acquisition policy to current theories, but sharpen the mechanism: the source does not validate a generic 'add 10% random reserve' fix because its nonrandom arms already had 10% random exploration and still failed. The actionable unresolved variable is reserve/arbitration strength and a positive coverage criterion, evaluated on a representative external surface. Do not relabel the paper's 10,000 fresh ground-truth samples as a reusable-holdout guarantee.
reproducibility_scope: Primary peer-reviewed full text and tables were inspected. The article links an OSF code/data package, but this invocation did not independently rerun the simulations or recompute the published regressions from raw OSF artifacts.
